hyps.why: With edge 5 already removed, cutting the direct input-to-output edge leaves node 3 fed only by edge 4 (or nothing), so the accuracy drop is much larger.
Replacing 'none' with a 3x3 conv adds an entire new path into the output, while replacing an existing op (e.g. a 1x1 conv) only changes an existing path a little.
If edge 2 is none, removing edge 1 disconnects node 2 completely, which kills the edge-5 path to the output.
Without the direct edge 3, the output relies on paths through node 1, so disconnecting node 1 is much more damaging.
When the node-2 path into the output is missing, a conv on the direct edge supplies capacity the cell otherwise lacks.
Adding a residual where there was no edge helps optimization, whereas replacing an existing conv with skip removes learnable capacity.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 outputs zero, so a conv on edge 4 has nothing to process and adds no benefit.
Edge 2 takes its input from node 1, which carries no signal when edge 0 is none, so adding a conv there is useless.
With edge 5 none, node 2 never reaches the output, so a conv on edge 1 cannot affect the prediction.
Swapping a strong 3x3 conv for parameter-free pooling loses much more accuracy than putting pooling where there was no edge or a weaker op.
